what: One-time compiler that reads TheIgorsProject's articulated layer (subsystem_index, design_docs, decisions, rules, tickets-as-pointers) and produces a deduped JSON index at CairnCommons/quarry/index.json. Every entry carries an UNPROVEN-PRIOR-SYSTEM stamp (Law 8). Deduplicates across the 4+ duplicate trees by content hash. The index is a lookup table — inference-free, compiled once.
why: Measured 2026-07-26: three ideas were re-derived from scratch in one session while they sat on disk in ~/TheIgorsProject (the Channel pattern, calving thresholds, and the node record envelope). Law 1's defect in its purest form — the resolver spent on re-deriving the settled. The fix: compile the quarry ONCE so /challenge's 'prior art?' question has something to search. Ideas to steal, not code (Akien 2026-07-26).
invoke: CLI: `python3 -m cairn.machines.quarry_index.compiler` (compile and write) or `--dry-run` (stats only). Prove: `python3 -m cairn.machines.quarry_index.proofs.test_compiler`.
how_it_learns: It doesn't, because the quarry is frozen (measured: 6 files touched since 2026-07-01). The index does not go stale from the quarry side. A scope error on ours would reopen the ticket.
filed_edges: (a) /CHALLENGE fired at /INTENT is the CONSUMER that makes this index pay — a separate node. This index is useful without it (a human or CC can query it), but the loop only closes when something fires the question automatically.
(b) THE 537 TICKETS are indexed as POINTERS ONLY (id, title, status, path) — not summarized. Summarizing 537 tickets ahead of evidence is the volume problem this node exists to avoid.
learns: Yes; it indexes quarry content and its coverage grows as new material is indexed.
